en: Advayavajra’s Works 3. *Mūlāpatti*, edited by MM Hara Prasad Shastri.
In *Advayavajrasaṃgraha*, GOS 1927, Baroda,
edited by the Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai;
and in *Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō* 10.
*Taishō University Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism Annual Report* 10, 1988, pp. (42/193) ^\S p. 13.
^M 42/193 % \msT (Tokyo color manuscript) [12r3] % \msN (NGMPP B 22/24) [8r3]
Having bowed to Mañjuśrī—the non-abiding nirvāṇa, beautiful with joy for the world—I shall speak of the fourteen root downfalls. (1)

I shall speak [of the transgressions]: through contempt for the teachers, through violating the command of the Sugata, through proclaiming one's lineage and qualities out of malice, and through abandoning great loving-kindness. || 2 ||
*IEB 323* “The Message of the Tathāgata”:
*dveṣād* in \M and \msN; *dviṣṭa* in \S; *gātra-* in \msT. Regarding *bhrātraguṇākhyāne* in \msN (IEB: *gotragaṇa*), p. 323 reads: “anger toward members of the feast family.”

In the abandonment of the thought of awakening, in the disparagement of the three vehicles, in the disclosure of secrets, in siding with [the wrong], and in the reviling of the Conqueror, the self, and the aggregates; || 3 ||
"Revealing secrets to unprepared people" (*jane 'pakṣe*) [or *jane pakṣe*];
"disparaging the Victor’s body of instruction" (*śāsana-kāya-dūṣaṇe*).

When there is doubt regarding the pure nature of the self and phenomena; when there is aversion toward those with corrupt friendship; when there is the superimposition of non-duality upon phenomena; and when there is the defilement of a faithful mind. (4)
The wicked one,
having arrived after a short time with [false] friendliness,
[attacked] the venerable half-verse.

If one fails to practice the samaya, or if one violates a woman who is the embodiment of wisdom (prajñā), it constitutes a root downfall; thereby, the mantra practitioner incurs a breach of the samaya. || 5 ||
In the practice of cultivation (*āsevana*),
regarding the failure to attain [the goal], there is a root downfall (*mūlāpatti*) consisting of not relying on the sacraments and vows, and disparaging women who possess insight.
If one performs that [action], there would be no accomplishments; it is a heap of suffering, Māra.
Such a person experiences the state of hell and intense, manifold torments. || 6 ||
And there may be those who go to the states of hell.

Having performed worship for the Guru according to his availability within the mandala, [one experiences] intense... sensations; intense sensations, various intense sensations. Then, having performed worship for the Guru according to his availability in the mandala...
And one should take up the thought of enlightenment and the vows of the Three Jewels and so forth.
The root downfalls are completed.
[The text] is completed.

A corrupt version of the Sanskrit for this list is found in the *Mūlāpattayaḥ Sthūlāpattayaḥ* within the *Advayavajrasaṃgraha*, Shastri 1927, p. 13. Among the numerous textual problems, *gotraguṇa* (line 5) should read *gotragaṇa*; *jane pakṣe* (line 7) should be *jane 'pakṣe*; and *iṣṭa-* (line 8) should be *duṣṭa*.

I have relied upon the various short texts covering these twenty-two points, catalogued collectively as To. 2478–2488, and particularly on the *Vajrayānamūlāpattiṭīkā-mārgapradīpa* (To. 2488) by Mañjuśrīkīrti.
